note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (only the ModuleLoadAccepted tail changed; cases unchanged) over the goyang fork, now committed in 66e87707f5 (go.mod replace github.com/ze-software/goyang v1.6.4-0.20261009101552-a3cf525c4f98, upstream PR openconfig/goyang#317). The STACK now meets the sentence 'otherwise, the assigned value is one greater than the current highest enum value': vendored EnumType.Set sets last on the first assignment or any higher value (len(e.ToInt) == 0 || value > e.last), so SetNext after an explicit -5 yields -4, and Loader.Resolve (goyang Modules.Process) no longer refuses enumeration { enum p { value -5; } enum q; enum r { value 0; } }. Ze's own producer (assignEnumValues) is unchanged and its tags still discriminate: TestRFC7950EnumImplicitValueFollowsTheHighest pins -4 after -5, 11 after 10 then 3, if-feature counted (2), two typedef levels down, each refused twin differing only in the value; TestRFC7950EnumValueRangeAndUniqueness refuses with ErrEnumValue an implicit value past 2147483647 and an explicit repeat of the implicit -4. Both tags' claims state only what their bodies assert, and the edited comments now say only true things (goyang v1.6.3 history, Ze's own refusals). Still weak: the module that proves the stack fix is exercised only by TestGoyangNumbersAnEnumAfterANegativeValue, which carries no RFC requirement tag, and every tagged positive sidesteps the defect (uniqueness positive uses r value -3; the implicit positives restate q -4 in a restriction goyang builds afresh). Under goyang v1.6.3 every tagged unit stays green (TestGoyangNumbersAnEnumAfterANegativeValue still carries no tag and the uniqueness positive still uses r value -3), so dropping the replace at the next goyang bump (which the go.mod comment plans) reddens no tagged test. Owed to reach enforced: tag that module as a positive of this requirement (or change the uniqueness positive's r to value 0) and record its discrimination against the reverted Set.
